927:
The following practices and procedures shall be employed by persons in the County in order to facilitate the collection of solid wastes:
(a) Refuse. All refuse shall be placed and maintained in containers as specified herein. All containers shall be maintained at all times with tight-fitting lids or covers.
(b) Standard Refuse Collection. All refuse shall be placed and maintained in containers as specified herein. Tree and shrubbery trimmings not suitable for bagging shall be placed for collection in secured bundles of 36"x24"x24" or less. Each container, bag, or bundle shall not exceed 40 pounds in weight. Refuse shall be placed at curbside for collection no later than 7:00 a.m. on the scheduled collection day, but no earlier than 6:00 p.m. of the previous day. Containers must be removed from curbside within 12 hours following collection.
(c) Garbage. All garbage placed in containers for collection shall first be drained of all liquids, and shall be wrapped, bagged, or enclosed in paper or plastic material.
(d) Household Trash. All household trash shall be drained of all liquids prior to its being placed in refuse receptacles. Household trash may be combined with garbage.
(e) Injurious Trash Items. All waste material of an injurious nature, such as broken glass, light bulbs, sharp pieces of metal, fluorescent tubes and television tubes shall be securely packaged or wrapped for the purpose of preventing injury to the collection crews or other third parties.
(f) Hazardous Refuse and Building Materials. No hazardous refuse or building materials shall be placed in any household receptacle at any time.
(g) Yard Trash. Tree and shrubbery trimmings in excess of that allowed for standard collection may be collected by private vendors.
(h) Trees, Shrubbery Branches, etc. Tree and shrubbery branches, limbs and trimmings cut by landscape or tree service contractors or other commercial workmen or resulting from land being cleared shall be collected and removed by those who have performed the work or shall be removed by the person for whom the work was performed in accordance with all local, state and federal laws.
(i) Household Furniture, Furnishings and Bulky Items. Upon request, persons requesting this service may schedule an appointment with a private vendor to collect normal household furniture and appliances, such as sofas, chairs, beds, refrigerators, washers, dryers, water heaters and similar items. Special collections are scheduled by appointment and are subject to a fee.
(j) Back Door Refuse Collection. Back door refuse collection shall be available subject to an additional fee.
(k) Standard Refuse Collection for Multi-Family Dwelling Projects. Standard refuse collection for multi-family dwelling projects shall be by on-site bulk containers. Entire rowhouse condominium complexes may receive individual curbside collection.
928:
The following activities are hereby declared to be unlawful and in violation of this Article.
(a) Reserved.
(b) Blockage of Drainage. No person shall place any refuse, trash, refuse receptacles, or containers on, over or near any storm drain or drainage ditches, or so close thereto as to cause such material to interfere in any way with such drainage.
(c) Unauthorized Storage. Any accumulation of refuse or trash items on any lot, property, premises, public streets, alley or other public or private place not permitted by this Article is hereby declared to be a public nuisance. Failure of owner or occupant to remove and correct any such accumulation of refuse shall raise the presumption that such person intended to violate this Article.
(d) Junk. It shall be unlawful for any person to place or leave outside any building or dwelling except as specified in subsection (5) any dilapidated furniture, appliance, machinery, equipment, building material, junked motor vehicle, or other items which is either in a partially rusted, wrecked, junked, dismantled or inoperative condition, and which is not completely enclosed within a building or dwelling. Any such item or items which remain on the property of the occupant for a period of 30 days after notice of violation of this Article, shall be presumed to be abandoned and subject to being removed from the property by the County without further notice. The County may charge the owner or occupant a fee for the cost of removing said item or items. This Section shall not apply to licensed junk dealers or currently licensed establishments engaged in the repair, rebuilding, reconditioning, or salvaging of equipment or furniture.
(e) Appliances. It shall be unlawful for any person to leave outside any building in a place accessible to children any appliance, refrigerator, or other container which has an airtight snap lock or similar device without first removing there from the lock or door. This Section shall not apply to any appliances, refrigerators or container which has been placed on or adjacent to the rear of the building and which has been crated, strapped or locked so that it will be impossible for a child to obtain access to any compartment thereof.
(f) Scavenging. No person other than the owner thereof, or an agent or employee of the County, shall disturb or interfere with any container used for the purpose of storing refuse pending its collection, or remove any contents there from or remove such container from its location.
(g) Scattering of Refuse and Littering Prohibited. It shall be unlawful for any person to:
(1) Throw or deposit any refuse on any public or private street or to scatter such refuse or litter on any public or private property; or
(2) Throw or deposit any refuse, trash, or debris in any marsh area, stream, drainage ditch, body of water or beach area.
(h) Use of Streets. It shall be unlawful for any vehicle transporting loose materials on any County road to transport same without suitable covers securely fastened to the vehicle. This Section shall not apply to the transportation of poultry, livestock, silage or other feed grain used in the feeding of poultry or livestock.

929: Editor's note— Ord. No. O-2020-09, § VI, adopted November 19, 2020, repealed § 2-16-256, which pertained to same—handbills and advertising matters and derived from O#2004-15.
930: Refuse collection shall be at a minimum of once each week.
931: Service to commercial establishments will be provided generally at a minimum of once each week.
932: Any commercial establishment or multi-family project that furnishes and maintains a bulk container shall meet the requirements set forth in this Article. Containers are to be kept clean, neat, painted and in a good state of repair.
933: Residential collections may not be made on legally designated County holidays except as the County may provide by contract for solid waste services.
934:
(a) Industrial Waste. Industrial waste shall be collected, removed and disposed of by any factory, plant or enterprise creating or causing said waste.
(b) Hazardous Refuse. No hazardous refuse shall be placed in any household receptacle used for collection of refuse.
(c) Building Materials. The owner will be responsible for the collecting or hauling of building material originating from private property preliminary to, during or subsequent to the construction of new building, alterations or additions to an existing building of whatever type or from demolition of existing structures. Such material shall be removed by the owner of the property or by the contractor.
(d) Hazardous or Liquid Waste. Hazardous or liquid waste or highly combustible industrial waste shall be disposed of in a manner which meets all federal, state and local laws and regulations.
935:
(a) Jurisdiction. The provisions of this ordinance shall apply to all unincorporated areas of Glynn County, except Jekyll Island State Park.
(b) Definitions.
(1) Business: Any person, wholly-owned corporation, individual, or sole proprietorship or other legal entity which engages in, causes to be engaged in, and/or represents or holds out to the public to be engaged in any occupation or activity with the object of gain or benefit, either directly or indirectly.
(2) Business Location: The physical location of a business. This definition does not include a temporary work site.
(3) Dwelling Unit: A building or portion of a building designed, occupied, or intended for occupancy as separate living quarters, with cooking, sleeping, and sanitary facilities provided therein. The term dwelling unit shall not be deemed to include individual rooms or suites in a hotel, motel, rooming house, or hospital.
(4) Mobile Home Park: An undivided parcel of land under single management which is used or intended to be used for rental or lease of spaces or lots and the provision of services for two or more mobile homes.
(5) Mobile Home: A movable or portable dwelling constructed to be towed on its own chassis, connected to utilities and designed without a permanent foundation for year-round occupancy, which can consist of one or more components that can be retracted for towing purposes, and subsequently expanded for additional capacity, or of two or more units separately towable but designed to be joined into one integral unit.
(6) Multi-Family Dwelling: A dwelling designed for or occupied by three or more persons or families living independently of each other.
(7) Non-homestead Mobile Home: A mobile home that sits upon property owned by one other than the owner of the mobile home.
(c) Assessment and Allocation. There is assessed upon every dwelling unit in Glynn County a fee for providing solid waste collection and disposal to be levied upon the owners of residential property in an amount to be set by the Glynn County Board of Commissioners each year. In the case of a non-homestead mobile home, the fee for providing solid waste collection and disposal shall be levied upon the owner of the mobile home. Each dwelling unit within Glynn County shall be provided with a solid waste receptacle unless the property owner elects to contract with a private vendor for on-site solid waste collection and disposal under subsection (e), paragraph 2 or paragraph 3 of this Section.
(d) Collection by Tax Commissioner. All fees for solid waste collection and disposal shall be assessed upon the tax commissioner's books for each year and shall be collected by the tax commissioner. After collection, the tax commissioner shall transfer the solid waste fee to the county treasury at the same time as county ad valorem taxes. In collection of this solid waste fee, the tax commissioner shall have the authority to resort to any remedy or right allowed by law for the collection and payment of county ad valorem taxes.
The tax commissioner shall prepare and mail to each owner of residential property and to each owner of a non-homestead mobile home an annual billing for solid waste fees. The property owner shall be assessed a solid waste fee for each dwelling unit on the property. This solid waste fee will appear as a separate line item assessment on the owner's annual property tax bill and shall become due and payable at the same time that county taxes are due and payable. Each year's payment entitles the property owner to solid waste collection and disposal service for each dwelling unit at that property location for the succeeding year. If the solid waste fee remains unpaid, the tax commissioner or an authorized designee, shall have the authority to issue a writ of fieri facias or execution against the property served. The writ of fieri facias or execution shall have the same lien dignity and priority as a writ of fieri facias or execution issued for county ad valorem taxes. Each annual installment shall become a lien against the property served on January 1 of each year in the same manner and same priority that a lien attaches for county ad valorem taxes. Any solid waste fee that remains unpaid shall accrue penalty, interest, and fieri facias, charges in the same manner and the same rate as delinquent county ad valorem taxes.
(e) Exemptions.
1. Sixty-two and Over. Any dwelling unit owned in whole or in part by an individual who is 62 years old as of January 1 of the service year and whose income falls below the federal poverty guidelines, as issued from time to time by the United States Department of Health and Human Services, shall be exempt from this solid waste fee. In order to qualify for this exemption, the individual must submit an exemption application to the County Administrator, or their designee, by August 1 of the service year. Applications for this exemption must be filed every year, including those individuals that have previously applied for, and received, this exemption.
2. Mobile Home Parks and Multi-Family Dwellings. In lieu of payment of this solid waste fee, an owner of a mobile home park or a multi-family dwelling may produce proof to the County Administrator, or their designee, clearly showing payment of a full year's fees to a private vendor or an executed contract with a private vendor to provide for on-site solid waste collection services for all dwelling units on the property for the entire service year. In order to qualify for this exemption, the owner must submit such proof to the County Administrator between January 1 and August 1 of each year. Applications for this exemption shall apply to the succeeding service year. If the contract between the property owner and the private vendor should be terminated at any time during the service year, the property owner shall give written notice to the County Administrator within three business days of termination of the contract. Property owner shall have seven business days from mailing such notice to obtain replacement solid waste collection and disposal service from a private vendor and to produce proof of this service to the County Administrator. Notice shall be deemed given on the date of mailing the notice. If the property owner does not obtain replacement service and produce proof of that service to the County Administrator within seven business days of the notice of termination, the Tax Commissioner shall bill the solid waste fee to the property owner on a pro-rated basis with the owner paying 1/12 of the annual fee for each of the months or parts of months remaining in that year.
3. Business Owners. In lieu of payment of this solid waste fee, a property owner that is also the owner of a business may produce proof to the County Administrator, or their designee, clearly showing payment of a full year's fees to a private vendor or an executed contract with a private vendor to provide for on-site solid waste collection services for the owner's business location for the entire service year. The property owner shall also submit a sworn, written statement declaring that they, as the business owner, possess the exclusive right to manage and control the disposal of solid waste at the business location. The statement shall also declare that the property owner possesses the exclusive right to deposit their household solid waste at the business location and that there is sufficient capacity to accommodate their household solid waste. In order to qualify for this exemption, the property owner must submit such proof to the County Administrator between January 1 and August 1 of each year. Applications for this exemption shall apply to the succeeding service year. This exception to payment of the solid waste fee shall apply only to the property owner's place of residence. If the contract between the property owner and the private vendor should be terminated at any time during the service year, the property owner shall give written notice to the County Administrator within three business days of termination of the contract. The property owner shall have seven business days from mailing such notice to obtain replacement solid waste collection and disposal service from a private vendor and to produce proof of this service to the County Administrator. Notice shall be deemed given on the date of mailing the notice. If the property owner does not obtain replacement service within seven business days of the notice of termination, the property owner shall immediately submit payment of the solid waste fee to the Tax Commissioner on a pro-rated basis with the owner paying 1/12 of the annual fee for each of the months or parts of months remaining in that year.
4. Disability. Any dwelling unit owned in whole or in part by an individual who, as of January 1 of the service year, has been found, adjudged, or declared totally (100 percent) disabled and unable to work by either the U.S. Social Security Administration or U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs and whose income falls below the federal poverty guidelines, as issued from time to time by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, shall be exempt from this solid waste fee. In order to qualify for this exemption the individual must submit an exemption application to the County Administrator, or their designee, by August 1 of the service year. Applications for this exemption must be filed every year, including those individuals that have previously applied for, and received, this exemption.
5. Other Exemptions. The Finance Committee may make recommendations to the Board of Commissioners to consider amendments to this ordinance to provide for further exemptions. Proposed exemptions to this ordinance must be placed on the agenda of a regularly scheduled open meeting of the Finance Committee.
6. Appeals. Whenever an application for an exemption filed in accordance with paragraphs 2, 3, or 4 of this subsection has been disapproved, the applicant may appeal the decision to the Finance Committee. Such appeals shall be taken within 30 days of the date of the decision by filing with the County Administrator, or their designee, a written notice of appeal specifying the grounds thereof. Upon receipt of the notice of appeal, the County Administrator, or their designee, shall place the appeal on the agenda of a regularly scheduled open meeting of the Finance Committee. The decision of the Finance Committee is final insofar as administrative remedies of the applicant are concerned.
7. Penalties. Failure of a property owner to notify the County Administrator of the termination of private solid waste collection and disposal service as required by this ordinance shall be punishable by a fine of $500.00.
(f) Property Tax Appeals. If a residential property owner files an appeal concerning the amount of county ad valorem taxes under O.C.G.A. § 48-5-311, the owner shall pay the solid waste fee in full.
(g) Partial Year Service. If construction is begun on undeveloped residential property after January 1st, the tax commissioner shall bill the property owner upon the issuance of a certificate of occupancy for the property. The solid waste fee in such an instance shall be billed on a pro-rated basis with the owner paying 1/12 of the annual fee for each of the months or parts of months remaining in that year.
(h) Severability. Should any section, subsection, sentence, clause or phrase of this ordinance, or the application thereof to any person or circumstances for any reason be held by a court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid or void, the validity of the remainder of this ordinance, or the application of such provision to other persons or circumstances shall not be affected thereby to the extent that any remaining portion of the ordinance may reasonably be given effect without the invalid or void portion.

938: All commercial establishments shall provide on-site bulk containers for the collection and storage of household trash. The bulk containers shall be installed so as to eliminate wind-driven debris and unsightly litter in and about premises. Any spillage or overflow shall be immediately cleaned up by said establishment.
939: All loading and unloading areas shall be provided with refuse receptacles for loose debris, paper, packaging materials and other trash. The owner or occupant of the commercial establishment or multi-family project shall place a sufficient number of containers in said area to maintain a clean, neat and sanitary condition at all times. The occupant of the premises shall ensure that all litter is placed in the proper container and the area is kept clean.
940:
(a) Receptacles within parking areas shall be weighted or attached to the ground as necessary to prevent spillage. It shall be the responsibility of the owner or his agent to collect the refuse and trash deposited in such containers and store until collected.
(b) It shall be the obligation of all persons using the parking areas to place any litter in receptacles or containers and it shall be unlawful for any person or persons to dump, scatter, or throw on any parking lot, any refuse, garbage or trash of any kind.
941: All construction and demolition contractors shall provide on-site refuse receptacles, bulk containers, or detachable containers for loose debris, paper, building material waste, scrap building materials and other trash produced by those working at the construction site. The site shall be kept in a litter-free condition. The number of refuse receptacles (not to exceed four bulk containers, or detachable containers) shall be determined by the size of the job. Dirt, mud, construction materials or other debris upon any public or private property belonging to a person other than the owner of the construction site shall be removed by the contractor upon completion of the construction.
944:
It shall be unlawful for any person to deposit or permit to be deposited on land under his ownership and control any refuse without first having obtained a disposal area permit as required by any regulation of the
Georgia Department of Natural Resources, the Federal Environment Protection Agency and the Glynn County Board of Commissioners.
945: It shall be the duty and responsibility of the owner of any private disposal site to keep the site in an orderly condition and maintained so as not to be a public nuisance of a menace to public health.
946: The Utility Director, Code Enforcement Officer, or other designated representative shall have the right to enter a private disposal site at any time during normal business hours for the purpose of inspecting the site to determine whether or not the site is in compliance with this Article and all other pertinent laws and regulations of the County.
947:
(a) No person shall set fire to, or burn any papers or other refuse deposited at any disposal site or on the grounds thereof, within the urban service tax district.
(b) No garbage or other materials, from which offensive odors emanate during combustion, shall be burned outside of any building within the urban service tax district.
949: No person(s) shall throw or place any building material, business trash, garbage, hazardous refuse, household trash, industrial waste or litter as defined in Section 2-16-233 of this Article in any ditch, stream, river, tidal creek, drainage collection system or retention basin that regularly or periodically carries surface water runoff. 963: This ordinance shall be known and may be cited as "The Glynn County Wrecker Ordinance."
964:
For the purpose of this ordinance, the following terms, phrases, words and their derivations shall have the meaning given herein. When not inconsistent with the context, words used in the present tense include the future, words in the plural include the singular number and words in the singular number include the plural number.
a. Car Carrier. A car carrier shall mean any device for the transferring of automobiles utilizing a flatbed truck.
b. Commission. Commission shall mean the Board of Commissioners of Glynn County.
c. Heavy-duty Wrecker. A heavy-duty wrecker shall be defined as a wrecker with at least 25,000 pounds minimum G.V.W. rating equipped with 16 to 25 ton P.T. mechanically driven power winch, crane and boom and having dual wheels.
d. Light-duty Wrecker. A light duty wrecker shall be defined as a wrecker with at least 10,000 pounds minimum G.V.W. rating equipped with an 8,000 point P.T. driven mechanically power winch, crane and boom having dual wheels, or a rollback body designed to carry vehicles .
e. Operator. Operator shall include the person owning the wrecker service and the wrecker service's agents and employees.
f. Person. Person shall mean a firm, company, partnership, corporation, or other business venture.
g. Wrecker. The term wrecker as used in this ordinance, means an automotive vehicle for hire equipped with hoisting apparatus and other equipment for towing wrecked automobiles or other type of vehicles.
h. Wrecker Service. Wrecker service means any person, firm, company, partnership, and corporation, which on a regular basis holds itself out to the general public in Glynn County as being engaged solely or partially in the business of towing wrecked or disabled vehicles for a fee.
